observations.epoch_band_state_and_other_notes: Spectroscopic orbital period from Armstrong+13 Table 2: 0.1456348(4) d; distinct 2012 photometric orbital-like signal is 6.870(1) cycles d-1. Gaia EDR3/Bailer-Jones geometric distance is 185.472 pc (p16/p84 184.563/186.448 pc); published Ridder+23 Table 4 value retained at 185.5(+1.0/-0.9) pc. MeerKAT detection is 99 +/- 26 uJy at 0.43-2.1 GHz (Hewitt+20); X-ray fluxes are Ridder+23 unabsorbed generic 7-keV MEKAL/PIMMS conversions from low-count ROSAT 2RXS, not source-specific spectral fits. Classification is state dependent: nova-like, Z Cam, and IW And-type behavior.

issues.competing_evidence: Hewitt+20 Table 1 uses Gaia DR2 inverse parallax 191.2 +/- 1.4 pc; Bailer-Jones DR2 geometric posterior is 190.128 pc (p16/p84 188.708/191.569); Bailer-Jones EDR3 geometric posterior is 185.472 pc (184.563/186.448). Ridder+23 Table 4 rounds to 185.5(+1.0/-0.9) pc.
issues.why_it_matters: Distance choice shifts unresolved M_G and radio luminosity; a uniform catalog distance convention may matter for population comparisons.
issues.needed_action: Review whether the community-facing scalar should remain the EDR3 geometric posterior or display the published DR2-based Hewitt distance alongside it; current wide-table Gaia distance and derived M_G use EDR3 geometric posterior, while the observational catalog preserves Ridder+23.

issues.competing_evidence: Armstrong+13 Table 2 gives spectroscopic f_orb=6.86649(2) cycles d-1 and Porb=0.1456348(4) d; its 2012 photometric orbital-like signal is 6.870(1) cycles d-1, equivalent to 0.1455604 +/- 0.0000212 d. Kato+20 describes the 2018 signal as 0.1456(1) d and cites Armstrong ephemeris 0.1456346(2) d.
issues.why_it_matters: Orbital, photometric, negative-superhump, and superorbital periods must not be conflated; the photometric peak differs by about 6.4 s but is low precision.
issues.needed_action: Keep the precise spectroscopic value in p_orb_h; decide whether the 2012/2018 photometric signals should be displayed as separate orbital-like signals or only in the measurement ledger.

issues.competing_evidence: Armstrong+13 calls IM Eri a nova-like CV; Kato (2019) identifies Z Cam-type behavior and IW And-type standstill-brightening-damping cycles; Kato+20 documents the 2018 IW And-type state. The 2012 negative superhumps indicate a disk-tilt interpretation but are not a WD magnetic signature.
issues.why_it_matters: A single static subtype would hide state-dependent phenomenology and could distort comparisons among non-magnetic CV subpopulations.
issues.needed_action: Choose a catalog display convention for state-dependent classification (for example, keep non-magnetic CV as primary class and list nova-like/Z Cam/IW And behavior as dated phenomenology); no evolutionary sequence is implied.

issues.parameter: X-ray flux and spectral model provenance
issues.competing_evidence: Exact 2RXS row has 41.93 +/- 7.263 counts and no accepted source-specific spectral fit; Boller+16 says spectral fits require at least 100 counts. Ridder+23 Table 4 gives unabsorbed 1-10 and 0.1-10 keV fluxes via generic 7-keV MEKAL/PIMMS assumptions and Galactic NH.
issues.why_it_matters: The fluxes are model-converted non-simultaneous estimates; presenting them as fitted source fluxes or temperatures would overstate the evidence.
issues.needed_action: Keep original ROSAT count rate/HR separate from Ridder+23 converted fluxes and retain the explicit generic-model caveat; no source-specific spectral fit should be adopted without a new analysis.

issues.competing_evidence: Armstrong+13 Table 2 reports 0.08 mag; Kato+20 Sec. 2 calls the 2012 negative superhumps 0.16 mag. The two papers do not establish in the checked text whether this is semi-amplitude versus peak-to-peak or a reporting/transcription difference.
issues.why_it_matters: The factor-of-two difference affects variability-amplitude comparisons across CV states and populations.
issues.needed_action: Inspect Armstrong+13 light-curve amplitude definition and Kato+20 Fig. 3/reporting convention; keep both values and do not average until clarified.

references.note: Downloaded arXiv PDF and text-extracted to tmp/pdfs/text/Kato+19_IMEri.txt. arXiv record lists related DOI 10.1093/pasj/psz130 and accepted PASJ publication. IM Eri audit: 2018 IW And-type state, three cycles of damping oscillation terminated by brightening; two periods 4-5 d and 34-43 d; behavior typical of IW And-type object and compatible with thermal-viscous disk instability in a tilted disk. Negative superhumps were not detected in the 2018 IW And state, in contrast to Armstrong+13 2012 novalike-state negative superhumps. No WD/donor component parameters measured.
references.full_citation: Kato, T., et al. 2020, IW And-type state in IM Eridani, PASJ, 72, 11.

cmd.uncertainty_method: Recorded distance endpoints transformed nonlinearly at fixed G; retain the recorded interval convention, including unspecified conventions.
